**Form of the original argument.** "Some good things are not cheap" is "Some G are not C." The conclusion "Not all cheap things are good" is "Not all C are G," i.e. "Some C are not G." So the argument swaps subject and predicate of an O-proposition ("Some S are not P, therefore some P are not S"), which is not a valid inference.

**Checking each option:**
- A. "Some Hunan people don't like pepper" becomes "some pepper-lovers are not from Hunan." The terms are swapped, so this has the same form as the original.
- B. "Some people are not selfish" becomes "not all people are selfish." The subject stays the same and only the wording changes. This is an equivalent restatement of "Some S are not P," so it is a valid inference and has a different form from the original.
- C. "Some good motives don't have good effects" becomes "some good results don't come from good motives." The terms are swapped, so this has the same form as the original.
- D. "Some southerners are not Cantonese" becomes "not all Cantonese are southerners." The terms are swapped, so this has the same form as the original.

Options A, C and D parallel the original argument. B does not, because it does not swap the terms.

Final answer: B
